title: By the Cornish Sea
summary: Written by the Cornish clergyman John Isabell (1851–1921) as his only novel, this two-volume story is set in the coastal fishing village of St. Enodoc in Cornwall during the late nineteenth century. Opening with a storm at sea, it follows Arthur Treleaven and Jenifer Trewhella from childhood and village schoolrooms through pilchard fishing, seal hunting, parish rivalries, a bank failure, and a voyage aboard the Annie Lee. Published in 1885, the novel makes extensive use of Cornish dialect, which is preserved here as printed.
omitted_from_reading: The printed tables of contents of both volumes, the title page of Volume II, and the publisher’s catalogue at the end of Volume II are in the JSON only.
notes_on_text: Originally published in two volumes; combined here into a single digital volume.
Cornish dialect spellings and punctuation are preserved as printed; twenty unmistakable printer’s errors are marked in the JSON and corrected in the reading editions.
